title: Finite bit construction: fixed-prefix helper470 retirement and five cut obstructions (no new kappa)
body:
[PR1128](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1128) leaves six rank-seven helper candidates at the fixed PR589 D/A/scatter cut. This contribution tests an explicit early-restoration mechanism: five candidates lose a required target dependency even at their least first restoration frame; helper470 admits a complete finite exception using rank two before rank seven.

**Status: finite construction and scoped negative result. No new kappa or selected supplier adoption.**

- Keep D, A, retained copies, scatter and the original B unchanged. Insert three gates after scatter, replace one cleanup donor and omit one cleanup gate. Every one of the 661 symbolic input columns is correct in both scalar directions.
- Helper470's frame dimensions change from `0 -> 1 -> 8` to `0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 7`. The other 660 frame itineraries are identical. Complete ADDs are 24,305 -> 24,307, MOVEs 2,911 -> 2,912, and paid local rank mass 5,129 -> 5,128; all nine COPY/ERASE pairs remain.
- Give exact target-access witnesses for all six single-rank-seven retirement failures, the five least-frame failures, and the working lower-frame exception. This does not exclude lower-frame preparation, later target-read cuts or other interfaces.
- Price the explicit two-slot relocation relaxation with all returned/consumed idle rank. It is favorable at the pinned bit exponent, but no physical window assignment or new bit endpoint is claimed.

Ali Romman's [PR1043](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1043) already deletes helper470 through an earlier source-boundary change and includes a hosted invoice. This does not improve that result or combine its savings. The distinct evidence is the unchanged-prefix endpoint and the six-candidate restoration classification. [PR1128](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1128)'s boundary model, Hanson Sun's [PR1079](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1079) census, Sagar Thakrar's [PR1023](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1023) hosting incentive, and DreamingOfClouds/eumemic's PR589/555 lineage are credited. [PR1179](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1179)'s kernel entrance is a separate mechanism.

Catalogue card `bit-helper-contract`: **scope changed** from the card's H2/K repair to an H4/terminal-frame investigation, after overlap with [PR1194](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1194). The donor's bit-supplier assignment is retained. [Task card and exact dependency pins](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2a6d342645ba919392c121f94f3345430afe0240/research/bit-early-retirement-cut/TASK.json) record the reason and bounded domain.

Exact research base: `49b3157d1d89adcef16df8be98445451672be5ba`; submission refresh: `dadfea6e8a78ff6ba901705f87532a71c6f5bbb8`, with identical input and the same selected PR1094. The sole live input has Git/SHA256 pins; external predecessor heads and historical context are in SOURCES.json. Seed8, bit-supplier track. Only `research/bit-early-retirement-cut/` is added.

[Proof, literal patch, certificate, scope and next steps](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2a6d342645ba919392c121f94f3345430afe0240/research/bit-early-retirement-cut/README.md).

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-early-retirement-cut
```

Expected: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/bit-early-retirement-cut outcome=completed`.

Local validation passed: registered Python3.12 replay; both checkers and eleven test groups on Python3.9.6; byte-identical receipt regeneration on Python3.14.6; selected-record integrity and all five selected-result tests; whitespace and source-pin checks. The two implementations use packed rows/Fraction geometry and set rows/fraction-free integer geometry. Tests include 22 star omissions, three retirement omissions, both cleanup errors, frame faults, source/receipt corruptions and read-only offline relocation. Hosted CI is separate; no hosted pass is claimed.

Unresolved: changed H4 cleanup admission, native 5/9/11-stage replay, actual owner/window assignment, packed precision/tape and outer/all-size obligations. The current complex supplier remains limiting. No full make verify, selected cold replay, or Lean theorem proof was run. Upstream and the selected frontier are untouched.

Smallest useful follow-up: test helper470's `0,79,186,513` path against one actual rank-seven idle window and the H4 cleanup contract before pricing a supplier. This is blocked by native/physical admission, not by the finite scalar identity. The README and task card also identify the exact later-target-read cuts for the remaining candidates.

Prepared by Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in reasoning, both implementations, tests and writing; Apache-2.0. Separate code paths do not imply independent human review.
